text.pZwXEK22YfQ:
St. Clair College Women's Basketball has landed a hometown talent. Maya Fuerth, a 5'9" guard out of St. Joseph's High School, is transferring in after two seasons with the Wilfrid Laurier Golden Hawks, where she started 14 games and averaged 6.5 points per game in 2025-26.
Before Laurier, Fuerth helped St. Joseph's to an OFSAA silver medal and earned WECSSAA All-City MVP honours, along with Basketball Ontario championships with the Tecumseh Saints on the club circuit.
Head coach Andy Kiss on what she brings to the Saints: an inside-outside skill set, sharp footwork, a willingness to finish through contact, real three-point range, and versatility on defense across multiple positions.
Fuerth will also study Fitness and Health Promotion at St. Clair while suiting up for the 2026-27 season.

The London Beefeaters needed overtime, but they finally got past their Highway 401 rivals.

Full article on our website. PowerplayWindsor.com
text.vimeo:1234711698:
The Windsor Lancers went into Kingston and knocked off the unbeaten Queen’s Golden Gaels.

Windsor beat the defending Yates Cup champions 25-22 on Saturday, handing Queen’s its first loss of the season. The Lancers (5-2) have now won four straight, and the Gaels fall to 5-1.

Kareame Cotton showed again why he’s in the conversation for the Hec Crighton Trophy. The Lancers quarterback went 17-for-27 for 284 yards and two touchdowns. He also kept the Queen’s defence guessing with his legs, running for 94 yards on 10 carries to lead all rushers.

His two touchdown passes give him 25 on the season, adding to the school record he set last week.

Fifth-year receiver Colby Ginn was his favourite target. Ginn caught eight passes for 182 yards and both Windsor touchdowns, including a 27-yarder in the second quarter and a 20-yarder early in the fourth. His longest catch went for 82 yards.

Kicker Alex Patrinos went 3-for-3 on field goals, from 34, 23 and 38 yards, and finished with 11 points.

The Windsor defence did its part, too. The Lancers picked off Queen’s quarterback Ashton St.Germain three times, with interceptions from Titus Lyles, Kevin Rakowska and Derek Anderson. Melyk George and Kage Bildfell each had a sack, and Windsor held the Gaels to 48 yards on the ground.

It went down to the wire. Ginn’s second touchdown put Windsor up 25-14 early in the fourth quarter. St.Germain answered with a two-yard touchdown run, and Jayden Gurzi-MacDonald ran in the two-point convert to make it 25-22 with 10:34 left. The Lancers defence held from there.

Windsor outgained Queen’s 447-328 in total offence and controlled the ball for 33:32.

text.-YYw0mOqOGg: 4th year hitter John Moate enters his final playoff run with the Windsor Lancers. He reflects on his last match at the St. Denis Centre and what his coach James Gravelle has meant to him throughout his OUA career.
text.We-b5Pc1tKI: Excitement in Komoka. Disappointment in Chatham. The Kings open the playoffs with a 2-1 road win against the Maroons. Jacob Howard's point shot hit the crossbar, post and counted as the game winner. Nathan Howard made 38 saves for the win. Dane Johnstone scored for Chatham.
text.TgBTvGxCTDA: Chatham Maroons head into the GOJHL playoffs as the #3 seed in the Western Conference. Rookie bench boss Kyle Makaric has enjoyed his first year at the helm. The former Maroons forward also embraces being back in the venerable Memorial Arena.
text.u2FQ67i4P0E: Nolen Vandenboom scored at 12:35 of the first overtime to help Dresden win game 5 in Lakeshore 2-1. Nathan Skulley scored with a sweet touch to give the hometown Canadiens a 1-0 lead late in the second period. Dawson Winchester tied the game on a penalty shot early in the third period. 16-year old Dresden goalie Brett Brochu made 46 saves.
text.jHFpU_O8UxQ: Windsor beat Waterloo in their regular season finale to finish 13-4. They tied with Western for 2nd in the strong OUA west division but the Mustangs hold the tie breaker. The Lancers will hit the road for the OUA quarterfinals at Ryerson March 2nd.
text.qGTC76Pbuyw: Windsor beat Waterloo to finish 10-8 for the regular season. They qualify for the playoffs and will travel to Ryerson March 2nd along with the men's team.
text.xLQTQVCsklI: Dami Alalade throws up consecutive blocks in the 4th set against Waterloo.
text.jnBpn5-aHbw: Jana Kucera won the OCAA scoring title with a 20.2 points per game average. She reflects on her accomplishment and the return of her twin sister Logan from injury.
text.Yq6EQcKZevA: Lajeunesse beat  the Blenheim Bobcats in straight sets to claim the SWOSSA single-A title.
text.-NQcL4h5o5w: Villanova lost the first set to Ursuline College during the SWOSSA final. They came back to win the next three sets but had to work very hard to secure the victory. The Lancers put in a great effort.
text.9d4QMN_L4LI: Horace Wormely took over the second half and lead Windsor to a 123-116 win over the St. John's Edge. He scored 27 while Tyrrel Tate added 23. The Express were strong from the get-go during Multicultural Night. They jumped our to a 9-0 lead and never looked back.
text.0g-0DX991Lo: The 9-15 Guelph Gryphons upset the 17-7 Lancers 62-59. It was a heartbreaking end to what was hoped to be a long playoff run.  https://golancers.ca/news/2019/2/20/lancers-upset-by-gryphons-in-oua-playoffs.aspx
text.MbridGTUPNE: The Essex 73's took game one of this Stobbs Division semi-final in double overtime 3-2 but it came with some controversy. Amherstburg scored what seemed to be the game winner late in the first overtime but players were called back to the ice after it was deemed there was a spearing penalty on the play. Essex head coach Gil Langlois says the linesman  made the call and according to the rules the linesman has that right. Hear from him and Addy's head coach Paul Bortignon.
text.mtnCKHKJ4mU: Holy Names beat Herman 77-51 to claim the AAA title. The Knights came out of the gates strong and never looked back. They built a 16-point lead after the first quarter. It was 24 by halftime. Galdo Tutu led the Knights with 20 points. Mehkai Barnett had 17. Dario Milojevic led the Green Machine with 14.
text.b-witJcuUZQ: The Kennedy Clippers beat Brennan with a convincing 60-32 win. The Clippers took a slim five point lead into the half. The went into lockdown mode in the second allowing the Cards to score only nine points. This is their fourth straight title (1 AAA and the last three AA). City MVP Akot Aken and Ardell Scott-Jackson each scored 20 for the Clippers. Zach Dilworth led Brennan with 12.
text.F6FpilQj9SM: Head Coach Chris Oliver honoured his lone graduating senior Pim Hurkmans, retiring ref Paul Carter and Assistant Coach Barry Amlin following their season ending loss to Algoma.
text.PIuioZGZ0Ik: 5th year guard Carly Steer ends her OUA career with a record 229 three-pointers. The Holy Names grad reflects on her time as a Lancer and easily named her favourite moment.
text.J5ZCbTZIBkw: St. Clair earned a straight set victory over La Cite but they had to work hard for it. The Coyotes made only six errors during the match. Te-Anna Stephenson had 14 kills. Amelia Oliverio had 9 kills, 6 aces and 5 digs. The Saints head to Sudbury for the OCAA championships and could be without the services of starter Jordyn Pranger who suffered a knee injury in the first set.
text.3sheP-W76Eo: The Amherst Bulldogs came out flat and found themselves in an 0-2 hole against Essex. Amhest gained a little momentum early in the third set  and got stronger as the match wore on forcing a tie-breaker. The Red Raiders led 6-3 early and 8-6 at the turn but could not close it out. The Bulldogs tightened up on defence and won the final set 15-12. The OFSAA AA hosts are one step closer to getting to the provincial tournament through the front door.
text.Yj9wCi9NgwU: Villanova played their best match of the season and earned a straight set victory over Sandwich to claim the AAA championship. The veterans in this group won SWOSSA two years ago and are hoping to make it to the championship tournament this season.
text.wxJn1iu8Td8: Windsor Express had a 13 point lead, then trailed by seven late in the game. They managed to comeback for a 119-114 win over Sudbury. Chris Jones sparked the comeback and led Windsor with 26 points. Ryan Anderson had 24. De'Andre Thomas was strong with 22. The win moves the Express within a half game of first place in the Central Divsion.
text.DW9hzj1MoXk: This one went to a tie breaker with Sandwich beating Holy Names 15-11 to advance to the city final. The Sabres were down 0-2 and roared back to win the final three sets.
text.XPnsotDlQ7E: Essex 73's beat Petrolia 8-2 to take a commanding 3-0 first round series lead. Michael Vieira led Essex with three goals. Adam Gaiarin and Josh Pope-Ferguson each pitched in a goal and two assists. Starting goaltender Jax D'Hondt was knocked out of the game in the first period after being run into.
text.VIbWBmJk2ww: Michael Knight makes a highlight reel dump during his last match as a St. Clair Saints at the Sportsplex. The graduating senior talks about his time at the college.
text.qdp4d0o96GM: Rob Lynch was honoured for his ten years as head coach of the St. Clair College men's volleyball team. Lynch tells us why he is hanging up his jacket at the end of the season. See the full ceremony held prior to his final home game at the Sportsplex.
text.HZ3TKE0QPBs: The St. Clair women's volleyball team swept Cambrian to close out their season in second place in the OCAA west division with a 15-3 record.
text.QrVUYCN3vVA: We start this video with a way too early first quarter celly by a Falcons player followed a sting of St. Clair plays. We end it with some hype. The St. Clair Men's basketball team upset Fanshawe 86-75. The Saints were quick out of the gate building a 20-5 lead early in the first quarter. They never looked back moving their season record to 8-10. With two games left in the regular season St. Clair has a chance to finish at .500 for the first time in seven seasons.
text.knzuHfxc3PM: The St. Clair Women's basketball closed the gap to five points late in the 4th quarter but dropped a 68-57 decision to Fanshawe. The Saints lapsed in the second quarter allowing the Falcons to outscore them 23-10. The Kucera twins led the way. Jana scored 18 while Logan pitched in 17. St. Clair falls to 10-8.
text.whHi4hShQ54: The Leamington Flyers moved three points ahead of second place London with a 6-3 win over LaSalle. The Nats have one game in hand as the stretch run continues. The Flyers like being in first but understand the division title runs through London.
text.ZqOGwCqzQio: Kennedy runs the table and earns the regular season Tier 1 title. The Clippers earned a convincing 78-51 win over Holy Names. Both teams came into the contest with unblemished records. Kennedy finishes 10-0. The Knights (8-1) face St. Anne in their regular season finale. Gatluak James led all scorers with 24 for the Clippers.
text.gjjXj6QxPHQ: In a battle of 7-1 teams, Tecumseh Vista came out on top 43-35. Milos Jovanovic led the Vortex with 11 points. Nikolas Godin dropped 10 points for L'Essor in a losing effort. Vista is on an 8-game winning streak.
text.sulfOmT7FV4: Here are the best plays we captured during the month of January.
text.Ucxww-MYTSw: The Brady factor is a big topic for the Lancers heading into the Super Bowl 53. Also hear their Super Bowl food of choice and score predictions.
text.Qoz2mxNrStY: The much anticipated game between Kennedy and Herman didn't live up to its billing. The Clippers entered the game 8-0 while The Grifs were 7-1. Kennedy went into the half with a 15 point lead and did not relent in the second. They rolled to a convincing 94-66 win. Herman was missing a couple of key players but did not use that as an exuse for the loss.
text.k79mwsiHOkQ: This grade 9 student plays with the poise of a senior player. He is the floor general for the undefeated Kennedy Clippers and is having a standout year.
text.HQsYCDO2mD8: Powerplay Video play of the week brought to you by St. Clair College Alumni Association. January 28, 2019
text.RPDBgI2Gh6k:
The Chatham Maroons beat the LaSalle Vipers 8-3. 

The Maroons were led by Nolan Gardiner who notched a hat trick. Jake O'Donnell pitched in with four assists. Three nice goals in this game. Check them out and hear from Maroons head coach Kyle Makaric.
text.5uwXN8T7Vv0: The Lancers split their four-game homestand and closed it out with a loss to Guelph. They are now on the road for the next four games which does not impress head coach Chris Oliver.
text.3tuqQfzmXIQ: The LaSalle Vipers took a 3-0 first period lead over first-place London and never looked back. The Vipers won 6-2 to inch four points closer to Sarnia for 4th place in the Western Conference with nine games to go.
text.r8fqczWfliw: Wicked save in overtime to preserve a 2-2 tie vs rival from Lakeshore. sports flash.
text.0camxWMIwM0: Lakeshore had its 10-game winning streak halted by the Essex 73's as both teams battled to a 2-2 draw. 73's goalie Jax D'Hondt made 35 saves and was stellar in the overtime session. With two games in hand the 4th place Canadiens have a chance to finish 2nd.
text.uEzl-KZu21k: Windsor Express gave up a 10 point lead and fell behind by 11 in the 4th quarter. Windsor managed send the game to overtime where clutch plays led the Express to a 138-134 victory over KW. Juan Pattillo was in beast mode scoring 40 points. Chris Jones had 24 and Tyrrel Tate 23.
text.T4utVsM2PUQ: Essex Ravens coach Glen Mills likes the hire of JP Circelli as head caoch of the University of Windsor football program. Having worked with JP and his brother Joe at Western he feels they will do great things in the City of Roses.
text.BFVDDOB-vy8: The rookie from British Columbia gets her first OUA kill in her first set as a Windsor Lancer. We salute Jenny Campbell with the Play Of The Week. It was a cool moment for the freshman.
text.rTqrSzxkASo: The University of Windsor lost four straight in November and went into the holiday break at 3-6. A weekend sweep of Lakehead gives the Lancers three wins in four matches in the second half. At 6-7 Windsor is within striking distance of third in the OUA west division.
text.bFpoE1t8t2s: St. Clair stuggled to focus early in this match vs Redeemer. The Saints got caught overlooking the Royals and needed to rally to win the first set en route to a sweep.
text.rXtxIWl77jM: Kennedy remains undefeated with a convincing 97-52 win over St. Joe's. The Lasers came into the contest on a four-game winning streak and losers of only one this season. The Clippers took a 23-point lead into the half and didn't let up in the second. Gatluak James paced the Clippers with 27 points. Kennedy is now 7-0 and tied with Holy Names for first.
text.FxJD13C5iMM: The University of Windsor women's basketball team is trying to build more momentum heading into the stretch run. Brock comes to town and is two games behind the Lancers in the OUA west division.
text.JiGM5BESpp8: This contest was never in doubt as Windsor disposed of Waterloo 72-50. Windsor's defence was tough holding Waterloo to 25% from the field while outrebounding the visitors by 10. Carly Steer led all scorers with 19. Offensive consistency was a concern in the third quarter but Windsor found its touch in the 4th to close out strong. Windsor moves to 9-6 on the season.
text.dzDWtXJMDsY: Villanova swept Amherst in a highly anticipated match between Tier 1 contenders. The Wildcats were undefeated heading in and held serve handing the Bulldogs their second straight loss. Villanova has sights on making it to the WECSSA final after being knocked out in the semi's last season. Amherst is looking to rebound before playoffs.
text.fK0pkF0FzHo: The Windsor Express hit the road for eight of their next ten games. The team has rebounded from the worst start in franchise history. Windsor has won seven of their last nine games to hit the 500 mark at 8-8. Ryan Anderson is 10th in league scoring and says the team needs to find a way to win on the road.
text.ZElYoQjg1Ps: The St. Clair men's basketball trailed Sheridan at the half by 14 points. The Saints cut the deficit to two in the fourth but could not sustain the momentum. Sheridan went on a run and closed the contest with a 104-95 win. St. Clair falls to 4-7 and are 8th in the OCAA West Division while Sheridan moves to 10-3, good for 2nd.
text.prTVbBLjI50: The Provincial Junior Hockey League invaded Windsor's Lanspeary Park rink to host three games. Amherstburg blanked Wallaceburg 5-0 in the league's first ever outdoor games. It was chilly but fun for all. The win moves the Admirals to within a point of Lakeshore for third in the Stobbs division.
text.cPA8JHx04aE: The Lancers beat Lakehead 8-2. Windsor head coach Kevin Hamlin says his team is prepared not to lapse in the second game of the back to back.
text.kX6s1wtt8O0: Villanova gets the upperhand on Sandwich with a 3-0 sweep. The Sabres kept each game tight but could not break through. The Wildcats remain the lone undefeated team at 7-0 .
text.F77OYdxgUo0: Windsor Express used a big 3rd quarter to down the Cape Breton Highlanders 108-104. Juan Patillo pulled down a game high 13 rebounds and was one of six Windsor players in double digit scoring. Ryan Anderson led all scorers with 34 points and feels Windsor needs to clamp down with a lead late in the game.
text.5zHTkyjFfnY: Battle of undefeated teams. L'Essor blew open a tight game in the 4th quarter to hand the defending A-champs Lamothe-Cadillac their first defeat of the season. Les Aigles remain undefeated in the tier-2 division with a 4-0 record. Lamothe-Cadillac is 4-1.
text.Fqsy6sk7tmo: Despite trailing by 23 in the 4th quarter the Lancers made a late push and lost 88-79 to Laurier. A Thomas Kennedy block and dunk are highlights in this video.
text.M6WeN4i85ww: Amherstburg native Erica Fryer got the start for the University of Toronto and backstopped the Varsity Blues to a 3-0 shutout in her return to Essex-County. The rookie netminder has a sparkling 1.73 goals against avg and two shutouts in seven games so far. The VIllanova grad made two solid saves with Windsor on a 6-on-3 late in the game.
text.iEMaLcqq_lY: Windsor opened the second semester with an overtime win over USport ranked Ryerson but were shutout 3-0 by UofT. Windsor has won two games in overtime and are still in search of their first win in regulation. The Lancers have struggled to win games but first year head coach Deanna Iwanicka likes how her players are developing.
text.ruX_bUV5ZJs: The Windsor Express handed the top team in the NBL of Canada a 110-102. The victory extended Windsor's win streak to three, their longest of the season. De'Andre Thomas scored 18 including a nice spin move fadeaway.
text.7P3UOW6Zq9k: Moncton Magic centre Nick Evans always enjoys returning to the city he once played for. He had 18 points and pulled down 8 rebounds in a 110-102 loss to the Winsdor Express. See the look on his face when talking about the NBL of Canada's top team losing to Windsor.
text.4loQ-brWF6g: St. Clair women's volleyball team had a strong first semester going 8-1 which leaves them in second behind 9-0 Fanshawe. They'll host a mini-tournament (Sheridan, Mohawk and Redeemer)  at the Sportsplex January 4-5th to get warmed up for a faster paced second half.
text.tJZYnUA1inM: There were many candidates to choose from but the Ontario Volleyball Association has tabbed Jimmy El-Turk to be their bench boss for the 2021 Canada Summer Games girls team. El-Turk has been the head coach at St. Clair for the past three seasons and guided the Saints to an OCAA bronze medal finish in 2017, their first medal in 21 years.
text.Z1b8Lgabmbw: Powerplay Video's highlights of 2018. These are some of the sports moments we captured throughout Windsor-Essex County. Enjoy.
text.S32vxSKMip0: There were many plays that made us go WOW but these are the ones we chose as our top 5 of 2018.
text.3Hff-ltUGWk: Ardell Scott-Jackson powers baseline for the jam against Assumption during their final game of the first half of the season. sports flash.
text.uMVKYCCEelw: Chris Jones is big addition to the Windsor Express. He scored 29 points vs London helping the team win back to back games for the first time this season. Windsor is 2-0 since Jones joined the team before Christmas. He played for Louisville and won the NCAA title with the Cardinals in 2013. He talks about his hustle play on defence after a perceived non-call on a scoring attempt.
text._-5RwLG4clM: The Windsor Express beat rival London 108-100 winning their first back to back of the season. Windsor is 4-7 heading into 2019. Hear from Coach Jones and newcomer Chris Jones. Ryan Anderson sings the song he feels best describes his team right now. https://powerplayvideo.ca/
text.KX2k2W2pQMM: Windsor Express beat their 401 rival from London 108-100. Newcomeer Chris Jones dropped 29 for the Express who are on a two-game winning streak, their first back to back wins of the season. They are 4-7 heading into 2019.
text.ZAka61laJOA: Emotional tribute by the Cardinal Carter Dance team from Leamington, Ontario. The dance was choreographed by Maggy Sonoski, Cassiah Prior and the students. Performed on December 7th, 2018. Song written by Smitty Kingston.
text.DmVas47xxAU: The Windsor Express are off to a 2-7 start following a 127-116 loss to Halifax. Windsor took an 8 point lead late in the 4th quarter but coughed up nine points in less than a minute following a timeout.  Horace Wormely led the Express with 24. Joel Kindred had 27 for the Hurricanes, who improved to 5-6.
text.N-GmYkFtn08:
Villanova sweeps Kennedy 3-0 pushing their regular season record to 5-0.
The Wildcats are tied with General Amherst for first in the tier 1 division and have only lost two  of 15 sets.
text.d7t-n4l7nx8: Gatluck James led all scorers with 29 points as Kennedy beat Assumption 87-47. The Clippers are 4-0 and look strong. They have big goals this season.
text.LoJPLbvGo0I: Chris Oliver has enjoyed his time hosting the University of Windsor High School Tournament. He has seen many talented players throughout the years and relishes the opportunity to meet and offer Windsor as a potential destination.
text.FyvDiC0oFRM: Boxing coach Cedric Benn has been re-elected by Boxing Ontario as the Vice-President of Competition. Benn is growing as an administrator while getting the best out of his athletes at the Windsor Amateur Boxing Club.
text.jw5y9LidEsc: Kevin Greenwood and Paul Carter are familiar faces on the Windsor-Essex hard wood. They were together again for a game between Herman and St. Benedict Catholic Secondary during the 62nd UWindsor High School tournament. Find out how many years they have between them.
text.agLWzBg7Or0: Herman bowed out of the 62nd edition of the UWindsor High School Tournament falling to St. Benny's of Cambridge 62-36. Dave Carson led the Grifs with 14.
text.T0DgQ5JGQLo: Kitchener's Eastwood Collegiate jumped out to a 12-0 lead early but Holy Names took a 6 point lead in the third quarter. The Knights couldn't hold on to the momentum and fell 50-45. Galdo Tutu for Holy Names and Ladera Ujulluobang for Eastwood led their teams with 20 points.
text.C5fM4nKXDbE: LaSalle Vipers give up a 4-2 third period to St. Thomas but rebound for a 6-4 win. Kory Silverio scores a highlight reel goal and added four assists to pace the Vipers. A.J. Ryan notched a hat trick. LaSalle hasn't lost in regulation in the last seven games.
text.HLBrszRtaoU: Kory Silverio scores a highlight reel goal for the game winner against St. Thomas. He finished with a goal and three assists in a 6-4 victory what moves LaSalle into sole possession of 4th in the GOJHL Western Conference. sports flash.
text.Ky-vxwL-4ss: General Amherst beats Massey 2-1 but the Mustangs pushed the undefeated the Lady Gens with scores of 28-26, 25-23, 17-25. Massey handed the General Amhest their first set loss of the season. Lady Gens are 3-0 (8-1). Mustangs are 0-2 (1-4).
text.J0Svou6N_Us: Adrian Ridsdale toe drags before scoring a nice backhander. sports flash.
text.Hp5KSApzOz4: Issac LeGood scored four goals while Joey Bellacicco had a goal and three assists to pace LaJeunesse in a come from behind tie. Leamington led 6-4 couldn't hold. Owen Semteh paced the Lions with a goal and two assists. Jaxyn Lafeber scored twice.
text.YyW2EbNC5Sw: Highlight recap of Dance-o-logy 2018. This year's theme: People's Choice. The school dancers took submissions from the public and interpreted them into well choreographed scenes. This is not a competitive dance group but they sure are athletic.
text.94w6DYB0tMg: LaSalle Vipers beat Sarnia 5-3 and moved into a tie with the Legionnaires for 4th in the GOJHL. The Vipers have four wins and a tie in their last five games. Newcomer Jackson Bernard made 25 saves in net and is 3-0 since joining the Vipers.
text.gvgK8kC2BJY:
Sandwich Sabres opened the sr. girls high school season with a 2-1 win over Holy Names. Hear from Emma Clements of the Knights and Marley Dunn and Chloe Dender of Sandwich. 
https://powerplayvideo.ca/
text.RZaERv-2Mlg: Power Plays for the week ending December 2nd, 2018. Athletes from Windsor-Essex County on display.
text.pyM_Xe_TX9s: Saints snap their two-game losing skid with a straight set victory over Sheridan. St. Clair heads into the holiday break with a 3-6 record.
text.sdxJrZXPduo: From Staples, Ontario, Friesen has been a pleasant surprise as a rookie outside hitter.
text.2VpMHLGpu-o:
Video from five set thriller. Niagara took the first two sets but St. Clair roared back to tie. The Knights took an 11-4 lead in the fifth and deciding set but the Saints found a way to win 16-14. 
more videos at https://powerplayvideo.ca/
text.2LAzZ81OTjw: New Windsor Express point guard Horace Wormely settling in. He led the Express with 24 points in a 116-112 loss to Sudbury on the road as Windsor drops to 1-4 on the season.
text.7NcldU4MAmc: The Saints erased a two set deficit and fought their way to a come back 3-2 win. St. Clair pushed the match to a fifth set but trailed 11-4. With the game seemingly over the Saints found a way to win the set 15-13 and take the match. Te-Anna Stephenson had 20 kills and 14 digs to lead St. Clair
text.X2_HBIMnL60: One of seven promos created for Scarehouse Windsor during their sponsorship of Powerplay Video.
text.GR8hX--2ZMo: Jordan Frasca scored a pair of goals as the Windsor Spitfires beat the Soo Greyhounds 3-2. It was the first GW in his young OHL career. The Caledon native has six goals and 12 points in 19 games this season. https://powerplayvideo.ca/
text.5Lg9pCGJ_-Q:
Essex 73's head coach Gil Langlois talks about the parity in the Stobbs division his season. Six of the eight teams are playing .500 hockey. 
Dresden leads the way. Essex is one point behind followed by Lakeshore and Amherstburg. http://pjhlwest.pointstreaksites.com/view/west/stobbs
text.yc7wpiUu0Is: The Windsor Spitfires beat the Soo Greyhounds 3-2. Beating the #2 seed in the Western Conference moves Windsor into 6th in the conference. Michael DiPietro made 29 saves and Jordan Frasca scored a pair of goals to pace the Spits. Windsor is on the road at Hamilton Saturday afternoon.
text.g-ofJ7DrExY: Hear from coach Bill Jones, Horace Wormely and Ryan Anderson following their 103-91 victory over The Sudbury 5. Juan Patillo led the Express with 18 points. Former Express Braylon Rayson led all scorers with 25. Windsor wins first game of the season.
text.bxG3YWU6f78: Sweet cross ice pass by Kory Silverio to Evan Ferguson who snipes top shelf. That was the game winner as LaSalle Vipers hang on to beat Strathroy 3-2 in GOJHL action.
text.9gLhFKJ4YzI: LaSalle Vipers Head Coach John Nelson talks about his team and the state of the Western Conference of the Greater Ontario Junior Hockey League.
text.7LQU7Txd19k: Joe D'Amore steps down as head coach of the University of Windsor football team. One of only four coaches in the program's 50 year history, D'Amore walks away after eight seasons at the helm. He took over in 2011 and guided the team to four straight playoff appearances. https://powerplayvideo.ca/
text.bugst9bvFEQ: Connor McMichael scored on the powerplay with less than 4mins to go in the third to help London extend their winning streak to 12. Liam Foudy was the first star of the game scoring 2 goals and adding an assist. Dan D'Amico and Curtis Douglas scored for the Spits.
text.cJJWxe6HoGc: E.J. Lajeunesse wins silver at OFSAA in North Bay. They lost to the top seeded O'Gorman Knights 49-39.
text.Gk2hfagGIZY: Men's volleyball team won the first two sets before Western turned the tide. The 'Stangs won the 3rd set and were leading the 4th before Windsor wrestled the momentum away for a 25-20 victory. Pierce Johnson led the way with 15 kills as he addressed a Western player taunt.
text.7k3M5YLO64w: Maurice Jones looked good in his return to the WFCU Centre with the St. John's Edge 13 points. His 15 assists were more than Windsor combined. He has fond memories of playing in Wndsor and has a message to the fans.
text.2S5yRsJun8Q: Leamington native leading Flyers in scoring as a rookie forward. The Oshawa Generals draft pick has 8 goals and 14 assists. He's proud to wear the home town sweater.
text.jsjt-aeNjsY: De'Andre Thomas talks about 27 point loss to St. John's Edge. Express fall to 0-2. Edge's Todd Brown Jr. and Jared Nickens led all scorers with 21 each. Reggie Hamilton had 16 for Windsor. https://powerplayvideo.ca/
text.Oc82_sBpZuY: Telloy Simon scored 18 points during Lancers loss to Western. After missing a year he is getting better but feels he needs to do more.
text.V3_f2nxEbGM: Saints lose a heartbreaker 77-76. Hannah Baker hits back breaking three with under 10 seconds left in the game boosting Niagara to victory. Rookie Noor Bazzi stepped up as the Saints erased a 16-pt second half deficit.
text.LWfqsXvl2DQ: Power Plays for the week ending November 18
text.utnQtJ_zaPY: Jana Kucera explodes for 33 points vs Niagara in a losing cause. She took her game to a different level.
text.zEcb6_eljxE: Hannah Baker drains a three with under 10 seconds left in the game to propel Niagara to a 67-66 win over St. Clair College.
text.GldvBIL4sdc:
Knights took a 14-0 first half lead and the defence took over from there as Holy Names wins a second straight WECSSAA title. 
https://powerplayvideo.ca/
text.rL3L7aMq_fI: Great block by grade 9 player Alisha Murray during SWOSSA final vs Wallaceburg.
text.i-93ajOKjxU: Highlight run by Wes Simpson during the WECSSAA final vs Holy Names.
text.bT8nvR0nHGM: Punt return by Herman is quickly thwarted by a big Kaiden Burdick tackle.
text.AK9P_RjmAoQ: Tartans advance to OFSAA for the 4th straight season. Clippers showed heart during the game and promise for the future. Wallaceburg fans travelled and made a difference in the Kennedy gym.
text.JQDUFXdfyh4:
Sarnia Northern travelled to Lakeshore and defeated St. Anne to claim the SWOSSA title and punch their ticket to the OFSAA championships. Sarah Woods expresses her excitement for the Vikings. Maddy Rozic of St. Anne shares her perspective on the game.
https://powerplayvideo.ca/
text.kvHLqNhEPRU: Head Coach Bill Jones talks about defending the great Michael Jordan when he played in the NBA.
text.GRZM6QMLlTA: Windsor Express gearing up for 2018 season with final combine.
text.mz_iKRFFcb4: St. Clair receives highest ranking since 1996. Saints move to 2nd in the OCAA and 10th in Canada after upset of Humber. Jimi El-Turk's team ended Humber's 155 game win streak with a straight set win.
text.-bz-9zGvy6s: Power Plays for the week ending November 11 features high school championships and St.Clair College upset and national title.

text.vimeo:1214390389: After two standout seasons at Cleveland State Vikings men's soccer, the former Toronto FC Academy star has committed to the St. Clair Saints. Correia leaves Cleveland State after earning Horizon League Freshman of the Year honours in 2024 and helping the Vikings capture the 2025 Horizon League tournament title, where he was named tournament MVP. text.vimeo:1210019910:
Maelle Dufour (L'Essor, Windsor Legion) wins the 2000m steeplechase at the U20 Championships this past weekend at the University of Windsor, crossing the line in 7:08.75 — over five seconds ahead of teammate Emma Rudling.
The Grade 10 standout wasn't done there — Dufour also set a PB in the 3000m, finishing 7th in 10:28.34.
Big weekend for the Legion program. �
#WindsorEssex #TrackAndField #U20Championships
text.vimeo:1209703340: Gianfranco Rauti has been building up and improving all season. He set PB's in both the 1,500m and 3,000m this past weekend at the U20 Ontario Championships. He placed 2nd in the 1,500m in 3:57.38 and 4th in the 3,000m in 8:48.52. Going into grade 11 at Villanova this fall, Rauti raced against older runners and held his own. He will now take two weeks off before turning his focus to cross country training.
text.vimeo:1209692581: A slow start in the women's 800m at the U20 Championships held at the University of Windsor. Anieu Chan or Massey and Windsor Legion broke away from the group with just over a lap to go and won with easy finishing in 2:06.21. Micah Carswell of Kitchner placed second at 2:10.19.
